title: kv-cache: adaptive spillover + defrag + scheduler heuristics to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: under high-concurrency long-context workloads the KV cache suffers from fragmentation which increases host paging/spillover and causes tail-latency regression. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes: (1) an adaptive spillover allocator that groups cold KV segments into page-aligned spill regions to reduce OS-level fragmentation and host I/O; (2) an opportunistic defragmentation pass that runs during low-load windows and compacts small free slots into larger contiguous regions; (3) scheduler heuristics that prioritize eviction/compaction for non-hot contexts and throttle batch admission for contexts likely to trigger paging; (4) telemetry and microbenchmarks to detect fragmentation growth and tune thresholds. The goal is to reduce host spill I/O, lower p95 generation latency under memory pressure, and retain throughput. Implementation notes: the allocator uses a two-tier freelist with size classes and a spill-region index; defragging is cooperative with the request runtime to avoid adding latency to hot requests; scheduler hooks are implemented as cheap scoring functions computed from per-context access frequency and vCPU residency. Backwards compatibility: on by default for dedicated/private runtimes but guarded by feature flag kv.adaptive_spillover (can be disabled for testing).

discussion: Miguel Alvarez (reviewer): This looks promising. Two concerns: (1) defrag timing—what prevents defrag from causing latency spikes? (2) does grouping cold segments into a spill-region make recovery more expensive?

Asha Patel (author): Defrag is cooperative and yields to active requests; we only compact pages that are not referenced and the pass is throttled by CPU budget. For grouped spill regions recovery is slightly heavier per-region but we greatly reduce number of I/O operations and metadata overhead; benchmarks show net win under realistic workloads.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Can we add a telemetry tag to easily correlate fragmentation spikes with specific model families?
Asha Patel: Added model-family label to fragmentation metrics and a dashboard snapshot in perf/microbench. Also added Linear ticket ENG-2050 for follow-up alert tuning.
Kenji Sato (reviewer): small nits on allocator.h naming and one race in admission_control—suggested patch applied in commit d2b4f12.
Miguel Alvarez: Approved after addressing nits and adding the e2e memory pressure test. CI flake on macOS presubmit; reran and green.
ci_checks: bench/perf: pass (12% p95 improvement on synthetic long-context workload)
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive spillover allocator, cooperative defragmentation, and scheduler heuristics reduce host paging and p95 latency under memory pressure. Feature guarded by kv.adaptive_spillover. See docs/kv_adaptive_spillover.md for rollout instructions.
perf_summary: End-to-end microbench: 12% reduction in p95 token-generation latency under a 95th-percentile memory pressure workload; 18% fewer host I/O operations due to grouped spill regions; average throughput unchanged. Production pilot on Dedicated showed ~8% lower cost-per-token when kv.adaptive_spillover enabled.
testing: Added unit tests for allocator size-classes, defrag safety checks, scheduler eviction scoring tests, and two e2e memory pressure harnesses. CI runs include deterministic microbench and an integration job that simulates preemptible GPU churn to ensure correctness during spill/recover.
